description: Most of research is failed experiments and grant writing. Ask about the failures, the funding, and the incentive structure - all three are openly discussed inside the field and rarely outside it.

questions.text: What has not worked, and how long have you been at it?
questions.lands_because: Failure is the daily condition of research and asking about it directly is a relief rather than an insult. It also produces a real sense of scientific time.
followups: How do you decide when to abandon a line of work?

questions.text: How much of your week is science, and how much is applying for the ability to do science?
questions.lands_because: The grant-writing load is enormous, universally resented, and rarely visible to the public. Naming it earns immediate credibility.
followups: What is your funding hit rate?

questions.text: What does your field reward that is not the same as what is true?
questions.lands_because: Novelty over replication, positive results over null results, volume over care. Researchers discuss this constantly among themselves and welcome an outsider who already knows.
followups: Have you felt that pull on your own work?

questions.text: What is a result in your field that you privately doubt?
questions.lands_because: Gets at the informal reputational knowledge - whose data holds up - that never appears in the literature. Handle carefully; let them keep it general.
followups: What would it take to settle it?
questions.avoid_if: The guest would have to name a specific rival or lab. Offer them the general version first.

questions.text: How do you talk about uncertainty to people who want a yes or a no?
questions.lands_because: Science communication under pressure is a skill scientists have had to develop recently and painfully. It is timely without being political.
followups: When did that go badly for you?

questions.text: What question in your field would you most want answered, even if someone else answered it?
questions.lands_because: The 'even if someone else' clause moves past career positioning to genuine curiosity, and closes the episode on what drew them in.
followups: What is standing in the way of it?
